What do you do differently season to season? Or, do you just let it do it's thing?
Do You make seasonal changes to your beard, or is it just continuous growth for you year round?

Considering it is 104 degrees here and my beard is close to as long as I will let it get.... I really don't make adjustments for season. I basically have a threshold for the shortest I'll trim it and the longest I'll let it get. Any bigger than a centimeter or two is a hassle.
The only trimming of the beard that ever happens is just to remove the little scraggly hairs that live to point out to the sides or get noticeably longer than the others.

Well, summer gets up to +30C and winter gets down to -40C so hell yes. Summer's usually a buzz down to 1/4". When fall hits I'll start growing it out and shaping in January. I have tried a long and unshaped beard with braids and ribbons, and curls, both of which looked great but took too much time to maintain. Last winter I shaved the sides down and kept the front long for a sort of tapered look that really worked out well.

This year I'm growing it out a bit longer to camoflauge my moustache, which looked terrible the last time I tried growing it out. I'd like to try something like Allesandro Manfredini's beard this winter, but I might have too much natural curl. We'll see.

TL;DR I grow it out and experiment with styles in the winter, chop it down in the summer for survival.*

*NB that +30 may not sound like much if you live in Texas, but for Canada it feels brutally warm.

My beard changes with my mood. The seasons don't change my beard. But, I also work out in the elements all day every day. So I'm pretty used to the extreme heat and cold both bearded and unbearded. But, when I do let it grow I usually just let it do its thing for as long as I feel is right. But, this go I'm trying to be a little less random twisted nature, and more guided man beast.
